Solutions/Shelving and structures

Heavy-Duty Cantilever Racking

Open-front storage for long, bulky and irregular loads.

Discuss this system → Read the FAQs ↓

Overview

How it works

Cantilever systems use columns and projecting arms to support items that do not fit conventional pallet racking. Single- and double-sided configurations can be designed for the stock length, weight distribution and handling method.

Typical applications

  • Steel pipes and profiles
  • Timber, boards and sheets
  • Long engineering components

Benefits

Why choose it

01

Clear loading face

Useful for long goods without front upright obstructions.

02

Purpose-built arms

Configure arm length, spacing and support for the stock profile.

03

Adaptable footprints

Plan single- or double-sided layouts around loading access.

Engineering

Design considerations

Arm capacity
Set by load weight, distribution, reach and arm geometry.
Column spacing
Determined by product length and allowable deflection.
Base and anchorage
Designed for overturning forces and floor conditions.
Handling method
Forklift, sideloader or crane, depending on the application.
Surface treatment
Selected for environmental exposure and specification.

Technical specifications are design considerations, not fixed certified performance values. Confirm claims with engineering and supplier data before deployment.

FAQs

Common questions

What is cantilever racking?

It is open-front storage supported by arms connected to upright columns, commonly used for long or awkwardly shaped items.

How much can each arm hold?

Permitted loads depend on the entire engineered system, load distribution, arm length, column and anchorage. Only the project load chart is authoritative.

Can the system be double-sided?

Yes. Double-sided cantilever arrangements allow loading from both sides when space and safety conditions permit.

Can cantilever racks be used outdoors?

Outdoor use may be possible with suitable structural design, finishes, wind considerations and site-specific safety checks.
